name: Violent Reaction
label: Revelation
lede: A shy straight edge kid in Liverpool made an oi-soaked hardcore record on his own, moved to Leeds, found a gang, and became the first band from outside America that Revelation ever signed.

eras.title: A one-man band on the Mersey
eras.text: Tom Pimlott was straight edge in a northwest England city where nobody else was. He wrote and recorded Violent Reaction alone, deliberately nastier than the positive edge bands, and didn't expect anyone to listen.

q: I wanted it to be violent and aggressive.
years.src: DxR: Tom Pimlott interview · Revelation Records
years.h: Tom Pimlott makes Violent Reaction by himself in Liverpool
years.p: Two demos, Violent Reaction and Session One, come out on Mind Rot Records, written and recorded by Pimlott alone. He wanted an anti-social straight edge sound.

years.h: Violent Reaction EP, still mostly Tom Pimlott
years.p: Released jointly by Quality Control HQ, 6131 Records and Mind Rot. The band plays UK Edge Day 2012 with a live line-up behind Pimlott.

eras.title: Leeds, and a real gang
eras.text: Moving to Leeds gave Tom Pimlott a band, and the band gave Violent Reaction its sound: Negative Approach and Blitz, The 4-Skins and Straight Ahead. Then came America, twice.

years.h: Tom Pimlott moves to Leeds and Violent Reaction become a band
years.p: Guitarists Tom "Razor" Hardwick and Charlie "Chubby Charles" Fresh, bassist Jimmy "J-Town" Wizard and drummer Nick "Skins" Sarnella join. Sarnella and Fresh also play in [[Arms Race|067526cd-2270-4e09-ade0-e0431b708de1]].

years.h: City Streets, Violent Reaction's first LP · Painkiller
years.p: Violent Reaction's first full-length, on Painkiller Records, with the Leeds line-up.

years.h: Violent Reaction's first US tour, supporting Hounds of Hate
years.p: The Leeds band cross the Atlantic to support [[Hounds of Hate|2a01d1e1-0a01-46b0-8a2c-2c839a6499c0]].

years.h: Callum Baird replaces Jimmy Wizard on bass
years.p: Jimmy Wizard leaves Violent Reaction; Callum Baird takes over bass.

years.h: Violent Reaction tour the US with The Flex, Pimlott drumming both
years.p: The Dead End EP comes out on Painkiller, and Violent Reaction headline a US tour with [[The Flex|1f7ba45c-19ca-48e8-b49d-eff0bfa1109d]] in support. Tom Pimlott also plays drums in The Flex.

eras.title: Revelation's first band from abroad
eras.text: According to Wikipedia, Revelation had never signed a band from outside America before Violent Reaction. The band toured the album hard alongside their sister band Arms Race, and called it a day within two years.

years.p: According to Wikipedia, Violent Reaction are the first non-American band signed to Revelation. The album is released the same day their spring northeastern US tour starts.

years.h: Violent Reaction co-headline the US with Arms Race
years.p: The tour kicks off March 31 in Washington, D.C., at Cafe Saint Ex, with London's [[Arms Race|067526cd-2270-4e09-ade0-e0431b708de1]], a Violent Reaction spinoff, as co-headliner.

years.h: Violent Reaction announce the end, then tour Europe
years.p: Violent Reaction say they'll finish at the end of 2016, then take a last European tour with Arms Race.

eras.title: Behind the kit in Arms Race
eras.text: Tom Pimlott stayed in the family of bands his project had spun off.

years.h: Tom Pimlott becomes Arms Race's drummer
years.p: Pimlott drums in [[Arms Race|067526cd-2270-4e09-ade0-e0431b708de1]] from 2016 to 2018, alongside Violent Reaction's Nick Sarnella and Charlie Fresh. Arms Race play their last show at the Damage Is Done festival on November 22, 2019.
